Status code stays 201 (late-hook snapshot protection). - Plugin receipt on `skipped_terminal`: `code: skipped_terminal`, `persisted: false`, `storedStatus`, `reason`; verb returns false; exit 1; failsafe cleared. - Hook statuses: new `system-event-skipped`, `turn-open-contended`, `turn-open-failed` (with reason `nonce_source_missing` or the server code); `turn-already-open` when a mint returns `merged` (same nonce). - Stop gate: blocks `turn_in_progress` (any ledger or registered turn still in_progress; in a host session with `unsupportedSince`, a turn whose close is captured as an `unsupported_session` failsafe record is warned with the cause instead, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001), `session_turn_completion_gate` (after S8), failed build after edits (existing), stale session (existing); blocks `turn_withdrawn_unclosed` (a withdrawn queued request still in_progress); warns on exactly the FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC005 list; re-evaluates on every Stop, including `stop_hook_active=true`, blocking again while turns are open and recording `stop_gate_overridden_by_host` if the host stops anyway; passes with `{}` and clears closed entries. Auto-close removed. Block text: `session_turn_stop_gate: <n> turn(s) are not closed correctly:` then one line per turn `<id> (<code>): <remedy>`, then `The stop gate never closes turns for you.`; each turn's remedy accumulates every unmet prerequisite of that turn, in this order: at least one model-authored action, designDecision, or commit (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002); `requestClass` (after S10); the terminal reviews the completion gate names (after S10, gate order); then the single close call valid for its status: `workflow.sessionlog.failTurn` with reason 'withdrawn before delivery' for a withdrawn request, otherwise `workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn` (or `failTurn` if the work failed), passing requestId <id>. Following a turn's remedy literally makes the next Stop pass for that turn, including a Code turn that lacks both model evidence and terminal reviews (`StopGate_EachRemedyFollowedLiterally_NextStopPasses`, `StopGate_CodeTurn_MissingEvidenceAndReviews_AccumulatedRemedy_NextStopPasses`). - Ingress mint (D1): `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint` (also `/mcpserver/sessionlog/...`), client `MintTurnAsync` and REPL `workflow.sessionlog.mintTurn` (hook and adapter callers only; no MCP tool), exactly as TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-005 specifies: first mint 201 `outcome: created`; same nonce in the same session 200 `outcome: merged` with the same requestId. Failsafe mint record: `{ method: workflow.sessionlog.mintTurn, params: { ingressNonce, queryTitle, queryText, model, planFile: None, todoId: None }, provisionalRequestId: pending-<nonce>, binding: { hostSessionKey, keySource, ingressNonce, requestId: pending-<nonce>, boundAtUtc }, plus the root-id envelope of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC009 }` (hooks send the `None` sentinels; a later update sets the real values). - Arrival bridge (D5): `sessions/<key>/arrival-bridge.pid` and the `turn-state.yaml` lifecycle below (no separate offset file); the bridge is the only minter on claude-code and claude-cowork, a fail-closed host session records `unsupportedSince: { causeOffset, causeOperation, reason }`, and a session-log verb applies, before binding, only the complete records that end at or before the transcript length it recorded when it started (D2). - Plugin per-turn store: `turns/<requestId>.yaml` (one file per turn, own lock `turns/<requestId>.lock`), `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml` `{ writeTarget: { requestId, deliveredAtUtc, source: prompt-hook | dequeue | absorbed-mid-turn } | null, openDelivered: [requestId], queue: [{ kind: request | system, requestId and nonce (request entries only), enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued | delivered | withdrawn, stateOffset, mintedAtUtc }], appliedThroughOffset }, every entry also carrying the root ids of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC009` (written only by the arrival bridge or a verb applying pending transcript records, the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, the close verbs, the failsafe drain (alias rebind), and the Stop gate (clearing confirmed-closed ledger entries), each write one atomic replace under `turn-open.lock`), `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/ended.yaml`, `current-turn.yaml` kept only as a read-only legacy status file `{ turnRequestId }` never used for targeting, the stop ledger as `ledger: [...]` inside `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml` (one file per host session, so an entry is added in the same atomic replace that delivers its request and advances `appliedThroughOffset`, never at mint; a crash leaves both or neither), all under `turn-open.lock`. No prompt ledger and no dedupe window. ## Functional Requirements (FR)

### Listing FRs

To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listFr
  params:
    area: MCP
    status: in_progress
```

All params are optional; omit to return all FRs. The result contains an `items` array:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  result:
    items:
      - id: FR-MCP-001
        title: Agent authentication
        description: System must authenticate AI agents via API key
        status: completed
        priority: critical
        area: MCP
        createdAt: 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z
        updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z
    totalCount: 1
```

Valid `status` values: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `deferred`.

### Getting a Single FR

To fetch one functional requirement by ID:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-getfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.getFr
  params:
    id: FR-MCP-001
```

### Creating an FR

To record a new functional requirement:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createFr
  params:
    id: FR-MCP-003
    title: Context search
    description: System must support semantic search across workspace documents
    priority: high
    area: MCP
    notes: Use hybrid search combining BM25 and vector embeddings
```

Required fields: `id`, `title`, `description`, `priority`, `area`. The `notes` field is optional.

# Copilot Instructions — QBrainAi

**Agent Identity:** When posting to the MCP session log, use the agent's actual identity in Pascal-Case for `sourceType` and the session ID prefix. Do not use inaccurate aliases, lowercase names, or legacy placeholders. Example: `Codex`.
For specific operational instructions (session bootstrap, turn logging lifecycle, helper command order), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.

## Response Formatting

- Do not use table-style output in responses.
- Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

## Terminal Usage

- Do NOT set focus to the terminal window.
- Do NOT write multiline commands to the terminal; use temporary scripts instead.
- Use **only `pwsh.exe`** (PowerShell 7+). Do not invoke `powershell.exe` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) for scripts, examples, or tooling.

## Session Logging Requirements

- Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for workflow and helper command order.
- Persist session log changes immediately after each meaningful update; do not batch unsaved turn changes.
- For each turn, include as much detail as available: interpretation, response/status, actions (type/status/filePath), files modified, design decisions, requirements discovered, blockers, and context references.

## Build, Test, Lint

```powershell
# Build (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 Compile
# or: dotnet build src\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp -c Debug

# Run all unit tests (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 Test
# or individual projects:
# dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug
# dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Client.Tests -c Debug
# dotnet test tests\Build.Tests -c Debug

# Run integration tests (uses CustomWebApplicationFactory, in-memory EF)
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.IntegrationTests -c Debug

# Run a single test by fully-qualified name
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests.QueryAsync_NoFilters_ReturnsAllItems"

# Run tests in a single class
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests"

# Validate appsettings config (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 ValidateConfig
# or: pwsh.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ./scripts/Validate-McpConfig.ps1

# Validate requirements traceability
./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability

# Markdown lint (docs only)
# CI uses markdownlint-cli2 with .markdownlint-cli2.yaml
```

## Architecture

**QBrainAi** is a standalone ASP.NET Core 9 server providing context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, and GitHub issue sync for AI agents. It exposes functionality via two transports:

- **HTTP REST API** — Controllers under `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/` (routes at `/qbrainai/*`).
- **MCP Streamable HTTP** — `app.MapMcp("/mcp-transport")` using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.
- **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; same tools as HTTP via `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`.

**Workspace model**: The primary host manages multiple workspaces, each getting its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` (not child processes). Workspace config lives in `appsettings.json` under `Mcp:Workspaces` (not in the database). One workspace is the "primary" — served by the host process directly; others get child `WebApplication` instances via `WorkspaceAppFactory`.

**Search pipeline**: Hybrid search combines SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses both with BM25 scoring.

**Storage**: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`). TODO items use a pluggable backend — either YAML file-backed (`TodoService`) or SQLite table-backed (`SqliteTodoService`), selected via `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider`.

**Multi-instance**: `McpInstanceResolver` overlays per-instance config from `Mcp:Instances:{name}` onto base `Mcp:*` settings.

## Key Conventions

### XML Documentation Required

`TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `GenerateDocumentationFile` are enabled globally in `Directory.Build.props`. All public types and members must have XML doc comments or the build fails (CS1591). Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test projects are not exempt: test classes and test methods must include XML docs that state what is being tested, what data/fixtures are used, why that data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.

### Requirement Traceability Comments

All source files reference their FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). When adding new functionality, reference the relevant requirement ID from `docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md` and `docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md`.

478: UC-1 Log each user request as exactly one turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId (only on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id or the bridge's single ordered source; on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails the host session closed under the equal-field rule, while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain reuses its nonce); the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9); on Copilot with more than one MCP prompt hook registered the hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and mints nothing (D11); on a host with no arrival mechanism every session-log verb reports `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6). 28: - Plugin turn edits are independent: opening, editing, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn's local or server state; concurrent edits to different turns do not interfere.
29: - Unsupported-session failsafe (operator, 2026-10-10: "If QBrain is truly not available, use the failsafe already in the plugin." and, choosing between a failsafe capture and a warn-only Stop, "1"): when a host session fails closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`), the model's session-log writes for a turn that was already open at that moment go to the plugin's existing failsafe instead of being refused, so the Stop gate's remedy stays accepted; the captured records drain at the next SessionStart through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original pair (C5); every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001).
30: - Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.
31: - Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.
32: - Hosts without an arrival mechanism (operator D6, 2026-10-09: "Adapters or unsupported"): every host gets an arrival adapter wherever the host offers any mechanism (prompt hook, transcript enqueue record, host-native hook, message-queue event). A host with no arrival mechanism is declared unsupported for turn logging until it gains one: its plugin reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb and writes nothing, and no first-sight minting is used anywhere.
33: - Plugin equivalence (operator D7, 2026-10-09, confirmed in chat "1 yes" for the requirement and its qualification posted by Codex in `MEMORY-PROCESS-007` at 17:48:48Z and 17:52:06Z): all QBrain.AI plugins keep equivalent functionality; shared capabilities, contracts, fixes, and behavior changes go to every plugin; host-specific adaptations preserve equivalent supported behavior; equivalence is limited by what each host's plugin infrastructure can support, no extraordinary effort is spent forcing unworkable equivalence, and each such limit is documented as a feature-specific capability limitation instead of being claimed as equivalent. A D6 `turn_logging_unsupported` host is such a documented limitation. The limitations live in `docs/AGENT-PLUGIN-FEATURE-MATRIX.md` (one row per plugin and feature: supported, adapted, or limited, with the reason and the receipt), updated in A9 and S11 and checked by a docs contract test.
34: - Ninth plugin (operator D8, 2026-10-09: "2 yes"): `mcpserver-grok-bot-plugin` is in scope like the other eight.
35: - Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, or the bridge's `dequeue` delivery), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`.
36: - Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.
37: - Copilot duplicate deliveries (operator D11, 2026-10-09: "Supported only if single hook"): Copilot gives no stable per-prompt id and separately registered hooks may see different `timestamp` values, so Copilot turn logging is supported only while the plugin's duplicate check proves exactly one MCP prompt hook across all Copilot hook sources; otherwise the Copilot prompt hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` before any mint, and the condition is a D7 documented limitation until fixed. One Copilot prompt therefore never becomes two turns.
38: - Node runtime floor (operator D12, 2026-10-09: "Keep Node 18/20"): the Node core and the TypeScript hosts keep their declared engines (`plugins/core/lib-node/package.json` `node >=20`; mcpserver-cline-plugin, mcpserver-cline-v2-plugin, and mcpserver-opencode-plugin `>=18`; the Cline application's own `node >=22` is unaffected). Exact review scores are read with a raw-token parser in the Node core, not with `JSON.parse` reviver `context.source` (absent on Node 20, V8 11.3), and the parser is tested on Node 18, 20, 22, and the latest release.

40: Request class
41: - Turn scalar `requestClass`: `Code` | `Docs` | `Chore` (case-insensitive in, canonical PascalCase out, anything else rejected). Required, enforced at transition to `completed` or `failed`, not at creation (hooks create turns before the agent can classify). Legacy rows backfilled to `Unclassified` (readable; never accepted on new writes from agent surfaces).

43: Review record (shared by `agentReview` and `hostileReview`)
44: - Fields: `status` (`Unnecessary` | `Unstarted` | `Running` | `Pass` | `Fail` | `Other`), `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness` (lossless decimal 0..1), `correctnessThreshold`, `completenessThreshold` (server-stamped, read-only), `reasons` (string[]), `reviewer`, `reviewedAt` (UTC), `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`. No `passed` bool.
45: - One record per kind per turn; latest write wins.
46: - Server creates both at turn creation as `Unstarted`. `hostileReview` flips to `Unnecessary` when `requestClass` becomes `Chore`, and back to `Unstarted` if the class changes away while still `Unnecessary`. Records past `Unstarted`/`Unnecessary` are never auto-changed. Legacy turns are backfilled `agentReview=Unstarted`, `hostileReview=Unstarted`.
47: - `otherNotes` with text is rejected unless `status` is `Other`.
48: - Strict per-status fields: `Unnecessary`/`Unstarted` carry no scores, reasons, reviewer, timestamps, or paths; `Running` requires `reviewer`, forbids scores; `Pass`/`Fail` require `correctness`, `completeness`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`; `hostileReview` `Pass`/`Fail` also require `requestJsonlPath` and `responseJsonlPath`; `Other` requires non-empty `otherNotes` (the Other reason; operator D4, 2026-10-09: "Other requires Other Reason be populated") and allows optional scores, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, and receipt paths. `Unnecessary` is server-managed only.

  "designDecisions": ["string array — decisions made during this turn"],
  "requirementsDiscovered": ["string array — requirement IDs e.g. 'TR-MCP-001'"],
  "filesModified": ["string array - file paths changed. Paths that resolve outside the workspace root require a foreign: / foreign-repo: / cross-workspace: prefix or a turn tag foreign-repo / cross-workspace / foreign-workspace (FR-MCP-SESSIONATTR-001). Completeness audits can filter those prefixes and tags. Forward-only: historical turns are not rewritten."],
  "blockers": ["string array — issues preventing progress"],
  "actions": [ "array of Action objects (see below)" ],
  "processingDialog": [ "array of DialogItem objects (see below)" ],
  "planFile": "string — required on new persist and replace: current plan file path (workspace-relative, exact, or ~/...) or the exact sentinel None",

}
```

## Foreign filesModified and commits (FR-MCP-SESSIONATTR-001)

A session-log turn for workspace W must not list `filesModified` or commit `filesChanged` paths that resolve outside W unless the turn explicitly marks them:

- Item prefix on the path: `foreign:`, `foreign-repo:`, or `cross-workspace:`
- Turn tags: `foreign-repo`, `cross-workspace`, or `foreign-workspace`

Unmarked foreign paths are rejected with `validation_error`. Relative paths are resolved against the workspace root (`..` that escapes is foreign). Empty workspace context (import/ingest) skips this check. Forward-only: existing rows are not rewritten. Completeness audits filter the prefixes and tags above.

Commit SHA/message without `filesChanged` cannot be proven foreign; mark the turn with `foreign-repo` when attributing another repository's commit.

## McpSession Module — PowerShell Lifecycle

```powershell
# Query recent logs at session start
Get-McpSessionLog -Limit 5

# Create session
$s = New-McpSessionLog -SourceType "Copilot" -Title "Implementing feature X" -Model "claude-sonnet-4"

# Add turn for each user request
$t = Add-McpSessionTurn -Session $s -QueryTitle "Add auth" -QueryText "Add JWT authentication"

# Record actions during work
Add-McpAction -Turn $t -Description "Created TokenService" -Type create -FilePath "src/TokenService.cs"

# Stream reasoning dialog as you work
Send-McpDialog -Session $s -RequestId $t.requestId -Content "Analyzing the issue..." -Category reasoning

# Complete the turn
Set-McpSessionTurn -Turn $t -Session $s -Response "Done" -Status completed

# Before compaction, persist the current session state.
Update-McpSessionLog -Session $s

# After compaction, record the compaction outcome and push again.
Send-McpDialog -Session $s -RequestId $t.requestId -Content "Compaction completed; recovered context has been restored." -Category observation
Update-McpSessionLog -Session $s

# Final push at session end
Update-McpSessionLog -Session $s -Status completed
```

13:   - Twin turns per prompt (e.g. `req-20261009T011653Z-prompt-b776` and `-c9a3`): MCP hooks were then registered twice (`~/.claude/settings.json` bridge hooks plus the enabled plugin `mcpserver@mcpserver-local` `hooks/hooks.json`). The bridge hooks were removed later on 2026-10-09 (MEMORY-FACT-003); a read-only check at 2026-10-09T17:54Z found no `hooks` key in `~/.claude/settings.json` or either `settings.local.json`, one plugin install, and one registration per event. The defect that let the duplicate go unreported remains: `validate-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1` wraps the `enabledPlugins` map as one item (line ~72), so it never sees the plugin as enabled and would report `valid` for a duplicate. A2 is therefore a regression fix verified against a fresh live inventory, not a cleanup of a current duplicate. Observed later the same day with hooks active: the prompt hook opens phantom turns for background task notifications, and each such open supersede-cancels the real turn in progress (`req-20261009T175347Z-prompt-dc63`, `req-20261009T175421Z-prompt-79dd`).
14:   - A new prompt cancels the in-progress turn: `Invoke-ReplSupersedeCurrentTurnIfInProgress` (`plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1:2131`, called at `:2300`). Canceled while being worked: `6067`, `5360`, `bc34`, `8ab5`, `11dd`, `ea25`, `9a7d`, and the plan request `e18e`.
15:   - Background `<task-notification>` events open turns (`-986f`, `-06ab`, `-290b`, `-4ced`, `-695f`).
16:   - False durable-write receipt: `appendActions` on `req-20261009T005031Z-prompt-d3a5` returned `code: persisted, persisted: true`, but the server turn has 0 actions. The submit terminal guard `continue`s silently (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/SessionLogService.cs:1606-1618`) while the controller hard-codes `persisted = true` (`SessionLogController.cs:71-86`).
17:   - The stop gate auto-closes turns as `'Auto-closed by PowerShell stop gate.'` (`plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1:1017`).
18:   - A single shared `current-turn.yaml` couples all turn edits, so edits to one request land on another.
19:   - Cross-session interference: this session's UserPromptSubmit hook reported `req-20261009T012640Z-prompt-b2ff` (a turn of a different ClaudeCode session, likely the Plan subagent's prompt) as "the root work turn"; hooks of subagents and parallel sessions share the workspace cache.
20:   - Hook-current turns can exist only locally (`req-20261009T013814Z-prompt-7ee0`: server PATCH returned "planFile is omitted", turn absent server-side).

22: Intended outcome: every user request is exactly one turn whose edits are independent of every other turn; every write receipt is truthful; every turn carries a `requestClass` and two review records (`agentReview`, `hostileReview`) with lossless decimal scores, a status lifecycle, and configurable pass thresholds; the server enforces completion rules; FR/TR/TEST/AC/UC are complete and traceable.
23: 
203: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC010 Queue lifecycle: a `queued` request becomes `delivered` (and the host session's write target) at `dequeue` (the head of the queue) or at `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`, and becomes `withdrawn` at a `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason; minting never moves the write target; a withdrawn request stays `in_progress` on the server until the model closes it (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009). A record that cannot be attributed to exactly one queued entry (equal content with no shared key: a `remove` matching two or more entries, or a `popAll` carrying fewer lines of a content than there are matching entries) is never guessed: the host session fails closed under D6 (the bridge stops before the record, `unsupportedSince` is recorded, every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until it ends, writes for its already open turns go to the plugin failsafe and drain at the next SessionStart (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001), and its open turns are listed with their pairs at the next SessionStart); a `popAll` whose line count equals the matching entry count withdraws them all. 206: - FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001 Prompts that are `<task-notification>`, `<local-command-*>`, `<agent-message ...>` subagent hand-backs, or only system-reminder blocks, payloads marking a subagent (Claude Code `agent_id`, Grok `subagentType`), and deliveries with `MCP_SUBAGENT_ID`/`GROK_SUBAGENT_ID` set open no turn, call no mint, leave turn state unchanged, and report `system-event-skipped`; classification uses these structural markers only, never the topic or wording of the prompt.
